text:
Maria: hey team — nightly CI is red, integration shard 12 failing against Hosted API. symptoms: auth 403s + streaming responses cut off mid-chunk. filing here before I start bisecting.

Kevin: ugh. any obvious error in the logs?

Maria: quick paste from the test run: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_client\",
  \"detail\": \"kid mismatch\"
}
...
ERROR: streaming: write failed: unexpected EOF while reading trailer
```

Olga: kid mismatch rings jwks rotation. Did we rotate the proxy certs or JWKS yesterday?

Maria: not that I know of. infra-deploy shows a platform config push 2am but no cert rotate noted. also the 403s are intermittent — some tests get through, then the streaming errors show up.

Kevin: could be two things: the auth cache still has old kid so initial token verification fails, and then downstream stream wrapper sees a truncated body. Can you repro with curl and the same token?

Maria: tried a manual call with the test service token and saw the kid mismatch. curl response: 
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\" https://hosted.api.redwood.internal/v1/stream
> POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-request-id: rp-abc123
< content-length: 86
{ \"error\": \"invalid_client\", \"detail\": \"kid mismatch\" }
```

sre-bot: note: nightly-run 3155550000 failed on shard 12: 6/8 tests. Incident tag assigned #ci-auth-2026-03-17.

Olga: can you check JWKS endpoint the Hosted control plane serves? maybe two versions active.

Maria: hitting https://hosted.api.redwood.internal/.well-known/jwks.json returns 2 keys; one key id is `old-kid-7`, other `new-kid-9`. tokens are minted with kid `new-kid-9`. but logs show verification attempted with `old-kid-7` in some workers.

Kevin: sounds like a caching/ rollout problem. Are we using a shared JWKS cache in the runtime? If so, some worker processes might have stale cache. Any recent change to cache TTL or env var?

Maria: Not aware. I can kick a grep across the runtime image for JWKS_TTL but quick ask: can infra rerun only shard 12 (quiet rerun) and also run a targeted rolling restart for the runtime pool behind shard 12?

ci-runner: rerun scheduled: `rerun --shard 12 --nightly 3155550000` queued. ETA ~6m.

Olga: while rerun runs — Maria, can you try a quick local repro where you drop the JWKS cache file and hit the endpoint repeatedly? might demonstrate warm vs cold cache behavior.

Maria: will try now. quick command I'm running: 
```bash
docker exec -it runtime-worker-12 /bin/sh -c 'rm /var/cache/jwks || true; curl -v https://hosted.api.redwood.internal/v1/stream -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\"'
```

Kevin: also pinging @infra to check if anything rolled out last night that could cause partial config load (they sometimes roll proxies one AZ at a time).

Olga: fyi if rerun still flakes after restart we should bisect between `main` and `release/2026-03-16` — last green before the config push.

Maria: rerun finished: same failure on shard 12 but only in container instance 3/4. logs attached to the run show worker3 attempted verification with `old-kid-7` and worker4 used `new-kid-9`.

Kevin: that's enough to confirm cache skew. two options: 1) force JWKS cache invalidation across runtime pool; 2) roll the pool. which is less impactful?

Olga: invalidation likely low-risk if we can push a cache-bust header or hit internal admin endpoint. I can run `POST /admin/jwks/invalidate` across the pool.

Maria: please do that and I'll trigger another targeted rerun on shard12 afterwards.

Infra action (Olga): POSTed `/admin/jwks/invalidate` to pool. Got 200s from all 4 instances.

ci-runner: rerun scheduled: `rerun --shard 12 --nightly 3155550000 --after-invalidation` queued. ETA ~5m.

Maria: new run came back green on shard 12. looks like cache invalidation fixed it. I'm going to leave the rerun results attached to the CI failure and add a short note in the incident ticket: root cause = JWKS cache skew after config push. mitigation = invalidate cache / rolling restart.

Kevin: rough edges but good catch. Can you open a follow-up issue to add a cache-invalidation step to the rollout playbook and make the JWKS TTL configurable per-pool?

Maria: will do — creating issue now. thanks all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident #ci-auth-2026-03-17 updated: status -> mitigated.
